blocks.source: Vol IV, Spatial Memory, § Coordinate Transform Expiry and Localization Drift
blocks.md: A coordinate frame binds a spatial representation to a physical body, but on an active robot that frame is continuously moving. Embodied architectures relate sensors, chassis links, and end-effectors through a transform tree, in which every frame has exactly one parent. A static drawing of this graph, however, conceals how rapidly its edges go stale. In the arm chain of a later section, each edge stores a rigid-body pose parameterized by joint angles, describing the machine only at the instant its physical geometry was transduced.

questions.q: The section **Coordinate Transform Expiry and Localization Drift** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: A ring buffer sized to the delay horizon lets the filter rewind to a late measurement's capture epoch, correct, and replay, and measurements older than the buffer are rejected.

A transform is a belief with its own epoch, so composing a stale camera-to-slot edge with current kinematics yields a pose the arm never occupied, and the lever arm, not clock resolution, sets the error.

A belief stops supporting motion when its validated error bound, growing from the evidence epoch, first reaches the task tolerance, and free space erodes inward from the unobserved boundary at a hidden agent's speed bound.
Space last seen free stays free only until an unseen agent could have entered it, so occluded free space shrinks at that agent's speed bound and blind crossings need site controls, not memory.
